rationale.conceptual: The underlying method (DFT geometry optimization with a standard functional/basis, followed by extraction of dipole moments, bond lengths, and formation energies) is an established but non-trivial protocol. It requires understanding the target conformer, building the correct initial structures, performing a relaxed dihedral scan to locate isomers, and computing energy differences. It is not a single textbook step but a multi-part documented algorithm, though no novel derivation is needed.
rationale.execution: The pipeline involves building the monomer, optimizing, constructing dimers, a dihedral scan, two full dimer optimizations, and then assembling properties and formation energies. That is 4-6 distinct stages with dependencies. Using an open-source quantum chemistry package (e.g., PySCF) adds some tooling overhead, though I/O is straightforward. This fits a moderate multi-stage orchestration.
